skill.name: create-unit-test
skill.description: Create and run Android unit tests that follow project naming, source set, Robolectric, and Gradle verification rules.
skill.summary: Guides consistent Android unit test creation and Gradle verification.
skill.author: AnySoftKeyboard

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md. Most Markdown backtick alerts are false positives for file names, paths, or source set labels. The Gradle examples are confirmed as external command execution because a project-local Gradle wrapper can execute repository-controlled build logic.

remediation.issue: Gradle commands execute repository-controlled build logic.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running Gradle commands, especially in untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: Command examples do not mention trust checks.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to inspect the repository and Gradle wrapper before execution.

content.value_statement: Android projects often collect inconsistent tests that are hard to run and review. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to create unit tests with project naming, Robolectric rules, and Gradle checks.
actual_capabilities: Plans happy path, error case, and edge case coverage before implementation.
Places Kotlin test files in the module test source set.
Applies Robolectric guidance for Android component tests.
Prefers fakes before mocks for maintainable test doubles.
Runs module or project unit tests with Gradle commands.
Directs users to XML test reports for failure diagnosis.
limitations: It does not decide production implementation details unless requested.
It assumes a Gradle Android project with testDebugUnitTest tasks.
It does not replace maintainer review of generated tests.
It may need project context to choose useful edge cases.

use_cases.title: Add Tests For A New Class
use_cases.description: Create unit tests with the correct name, package path, and source set.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Test Style
use_cases.description: Apply consistent Arrange-Act-Assert structure, fake-first test doubles, and Robolectric usage.

use_cases.title: Investigate Unit Test Failures
use_cases.description: Run the relevant Gradle task and inspect XML test reports for failure details.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic Unit Test

prompt_templates.title: Cover Edge Cases
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-unit-test skill to identify likely error cases and edge cases before writing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Test Android Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-unit-test skill to add Robolectric-based unit tests for this Android component.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Failing Tests

output_examples.input: Request to add unit tests for an Android utility class.
output: A focused test plan covering main behavior and likely errors.
A new Kotlin test file in the module test source set.
A Gradle verification step for the related module.

output_examples.input: Request to investigate a failing Android unit test.
output: The relevant Gradle task to run after confirmation.
The XML report location to inspect for failure details.
A short diagnosis based on the reported assertion or exception.

best_practices: Confirm the target module and package before creating the test file.
Use fakes when they keep tests clear and deterministic.
Run the smallest relevant Gradle test task before broader verification.
anti_patterns: Putting local unit tests in the instrumentation test source set by default.
Adding brittle mocks when a simple fake would be clearer.
Changing production behavior while only being asked to add tests.

faq.question: What type of project is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is designed for Android Gradle projects that use Kotlin unit tests.

faq.question: Does it support Robolectric tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires Robolectric when testing Android components in local unit tests.

faq.question: Can it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It can recommend Gradle commands, but command execution should require user confirmation.

faq.question: Does it create instrumentation tests?
faq.answer: No. It defaults to local unit tests unless instrumentation tests are specifically requested.

faq.question: How does it handle test doubles?
faq.answer: It prefers fakes first and uses mocks only when fakes are too complex.

faq.question: How are failures investigated?
faq.answer: It points to Gradle XML test reports and uses those details to diagnose failures.
